dct_description_sm: The Centre of Expertise in Marine Mammalogy (CEMAM) has been charged with identifying marine mammal research priorities and increasing the visibility of its marine mammal program. Marine mammal scientists, and CEMAM, have many reasons for performing research activities. This research involves national and international collaborations with industry, universities, non-government organizations (NGOs), and other government agencies. There are many commitments to the Species at Risk Act (SARA), as many marine mammals in Canada are threatened or endangered, and thus advice needs to be provided relating to recovery potential. Research is also required under the Oceans Act, under which Marine Protected Areas are created, and the Fisheries Act, which has a section specifically for marine mammals, to ensure protection. Several species of marine mammal are hunted in Canada, both commercially and for subsistence. The Marine Mammal Regulations of the Fisheries Act aims to regulate and monitor these hunts. It is the responsibility of CEMAM to conduct surveys and assessments in order to provide abundance estimates and total allowable catch (TAC) levels for these hunts. The specific purpose of this study is to do aerial surveys to determine population numbers and distribution of marine mammals. ( from http://www.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/science/coe-cde/cemam/reference-eng.pdf)
dct_title_s: Survey of marine mammals across the Canadian Arctic
